prompts.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Input image is the edit target: the approved Threadbound base outfit FRONT reference. Make ONE small change only.
Add an EMPTY low-profile grapple attachment saddle to the character's LEFT leather forearm bracer, which is on the RIGHT side of this front-facing image. It lies on the palm-facing inside forearm, lengthwise between elbow and wrist, centered on the bracer. Design: a small worn brown stitched leather rectangular saddle, two restrained dull-bronze retaining loops along the forearm axis and a small empty needle retaining clip near the wrist, made to accept a separate compact braided rope coil and sewing needle. It looks like a practical handcrafted leather-and-bronze mounting point, not machinery. All retaining loops are EMPTY. Keep it compact and flush, within the existing forearm outline, clear of exposed elbow and wrist joints.
Preserve EXACTLY everything else: same front T-pose with open palms toward viewer, centered full-body 1254-square composition white background, same proportions, blank ivory-wood stitched face with no eyes/mouth/nose, hands, cowl, charcoal-indigo cloth, ragged sleeves and tunic, warm construction stitching, brown sash, pouch on viewer LEFT, pants covering knees down toward compact mid-shin boots with only a narrow plain-wood shin band. Same reference colors, texture and lighting. Other bracer on viewer LEFT is unchanged. No attached grapple, rope, coil, needle, hook, shield, sword, new embroidery motif, arrows, captions, inset or watermark. This is a clean single-character modeling reference, not a concept board.

Use case: precise-object-edit.
Input 1 is the edit target: approved Threadbound BACK T-pose reference. Input 2 is the matching FRONT reference showing the new empty grapple saddle.
Produce one clean single-character BACK T-pose modeling reference. Match image 1 exactly except for any subtle edge visibility of the new left bracer saddle. The grapple attachment saddle is built into the palm-facing INSIDE of the character's LEFT forearm, which is on the LEFT side of the BACK image. Because this camera sees the backs of the hands and dorsal forearms, the main bronze loops/plate shown in front image 2 must be hidden on the far side of this left bracer; at most a tiny leather saddle edge may peek around its lower edge. Do NOT put a second mounting plate on the visible dorsal side. Right bracer stays plain.
Preserve full-body pose, original proportions, framing white background, doll body identity, blank ivory wood stitched head, dorsal segmented wooden hands, charcoal-indigo clothes with gold construction stitches, knee-covering continuous ragged pants, narrow plain-wood shin band, compact mid-shin boots with heels visible, cowl's rear folds and pouch on viewer RIGHT. No palms facing viewer in a back view. No new gear, no attached rope, needle, coil, hook, shield, sword, embroidery designs, text, labels or watermark. Same image dimensions and lighting.

Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset: Threadbound BASE grapple SEWING NEEDLE isolated component reference, for a separate articulated prop model.
Input image 1 supplies the existing needle design: preserve the recognizable large elongated oval eye above a long tapered straight pointed metal blade, no fishhook or prongs. Image 2 supplies only current doll/outfit rendering style and handcrafted material finish.
Show exactly ONE complete needle centered vertically on a clean warm-white background, point down, entire outline visible with generous margin. Large simple oval eye at the top, smooth worn dull silver/steel, long straight taper, sturdy enough for stylized 3D game use, subtly beveled edge, hand-forged irregularities but not filigree. It is a sewing needle / bodkin, not a sword, harpoon or mechanical launcher. No handle or crossguard. The needle's intended total length is about half the doll's bracer length, not a full forearm sword; show no scale character. Preserve natural metallic neutral color so Identity colors do not recolor the steel.
Crucial: remove all rope, knots and other sprites from input 1. The eye must be OPEN and EMPTY. No coil, rope tail, bracer, hand, body, detached pieces, extra views, text, arrows, watermark or frame. Soft neutral studio lighting, same illustrated tactile game concept style as input 2, crisp simple silhouette, not a photorealistic product photograph.

Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset: Threadbound BASE grapple stowed ROPE COIL isolated prop reference.
Input 1 is material/style guidance for golden flax twisted rope, not the composition: do NOT reproduce disconnected horizontal rope sprites. Input 2 gives the current handcrafted doll/outfit illustration style and brown leather/bronze bracer mounting saddle.
Create one SINGLE coherent compact flattened OVAL COIL of flax rope, about five neatly gathered oval loops wound from one continuous rope. Long oval axis runs horizontally. A simple small dark-brown leather binding wraps the midpoint of the bundle, keeping the nested oval loops together; its underside has a compact flat leather tongue intended to slip under two retaining loops on the doll's inner-forearm mount. The natural golden-tan rope has readable large twisted strands, no excessively furry microdetail. Leave a short SINGLE loose lead gently curving to the right with its end fully visible and not knotted; it will later tie through a separate sewing needle's eye. No needle is present here.
Show a clear slightly elevated three-quarter product angle so the flattened coil's small thickness and binding are understandable. The prop's intended length is about two thirds of the doll's bracer length and its width narrower than the bracer. No mechanical spool/reel, no winch, no launcher, no fishing hook, no extra buckles or ornament. Compact clean silhouette, practical handbound starter equipment, neutral soft lighting, subtly painted tactile 3D-game concept finish matching input 2.
Isolated warm-white background, whole coil and short lead visible with generous margins. No bracer, hand, body, needle, separate components, extra views, exploded diagram, labels, arrows, text, frame or watermark.

Use case: compositing.
Asset: Threadbound BASE grapple mounting and stowed assembly review board.
Inputs: 1 approved current base doll front with empty LEFT inner-forearm leather/brass mounting saddle; 2 isolated base rope coil with leather binding and flat underside tongue; 3 isolated base metal sewing needle with long open oval eye. Preserve these exact component designs.
Create one clean landscape board, TWO close-up views stacked vertically, same scale and same camera. Only a LEFT forearm and open wooden hand from the doll, no whole character. Elbow is at LEFT, wrist and open palm at RIGHT. Camera looks at palm-facing INNER forearm so the mount is visible. Retain the source's tapered brown leather bracer, exposed wooden ball elbow and wrist, ivory segmented wooden hand and fingers. Large components with plenty of blank margin, handcrafted painted game-concept style, soft neutral lighting, warm-white background.
Top row label exactly "EMPTY MOUNT": show the slim brown stitched leather saddle and two small dull-bronze retaining loops and empty needle clip, like input 1. Empty.
Bottom row label exactly "BASE GRAPPLE ATTACHED": SAME forearm, SAME mounting saddle. Attach input 2's leather-tied compact oval rope coil lengthwise over the saddle, with its underside leather tongue under the mount loops. Its length is about 60 percent of the bracer length, width about 55 percent of bracer width, low profile. Beside the coil, clip ONE input 3 metal sewing needle parallel to the forearm, eye toward the elbow LEFT and point toward wrist RIGHT. Needle length about 50 percent of bracer length, fully inside bracer endpoints, never extending onto wrist/hand. A short visible flexible rope lead runs from coil and ties through the needle eye; no long loose tails. The mount, stowed coil, and needle must remain distinct readable components with space around elbow and wrist. Practical handbound beginner equipment, not a mechanical launcher or gun.
No shield or sword, extra tools, duplicated needle, hooks, spools, glowing effects, new armor, purple colors, diagrams/arrows, dimensions, invented symbols, additional text or watermark. The point of the board is verifying compact fit and shared attachment, not redesigning glove shape.

Use case: identity-preserve.
Asset type: preview-only character palette comparison sheet for Threadbound.
Input image 1 is the exact current base gear design and doll identity to preserve.
Create ONE polished wide comparison board showing FOUR faithful full-body copies of this SAME character, in a tidy 2 by 2 grid on a clean warm-white background. Every character is at identical scale in the reference's straight-on front T-pose, arms straight horizontally, open palms forward, with generous gutters so fingers never overlap a neighboring character. Keep the reference's illustrated game-concept finish. Large clear characters, restrained labels above each panel.
Change only the cloth palette and selected existing stitch accents. Exact same silhouette, garment construction, garment lengths, proportions, ivory wood body, blank oval stitched head without facial features, sleeve length, exposed elbow joints, leather bracers, sash, pouch, ragged continuous knee-covering trousers, narrow plain-wood shin gap and compact mid-shin boots across ALL FOUR panels. Leather bracers, boots, sash and pouch remain the SAME warm worn brown in every panel; wooden head/hands/joints remain SAME pale ivory wood; metal remains natural. Do not tint the entire character. Do not add gear or grapples, armor, weapons, symbols, floating panels, embroidery motifs, hoods, faces, knee openings or longer boots.
Panel upper left label exactly "BASE": reference charcoal-grey cloth with warm flax stitching.
Panel upper right label exactly "RED IDENTITY": muted rich brick-crimson tunic and sleeves, slightly darker wine-red cowl and trousers, restrained warm flax construction stitching; natural brown leather unchanged.
Panel lower left label exactly "BLUE IDENTITY": muted deep blue tunic and sleeves, slightly darker blue-teal cowl and trousers, restrained pale flax construction stitching; natural brown leather unchanged.
Panel lower right label exactly "YELLOW IDENTITY": muted ochre-gold tunic and sleeves, slightly darker olive-ochre cowl and trousers, restrained pale flax construction stitching; natural brown leather unchanged.
Important: these are four Identity color applications to ONE base equipment silhouette, not four different equipment sets. Retain all fabric wear and folds but no excessive baked shadow or colored environmental lighting. Keep each recolor elegant and readable at game size. Title at top exactly "SAME GEAR, DIFFERENT IDENTITY". No other text, arrows, legends, swatches or watermark.
